sentences.text: The criminal law has been set into motion based on the first information statement of Deepak L.

The gist of the prosecution case is that on 26-08-2022 the CW-1 received credible information and conducted raid along with CW 8 in the presence of CW 2 and 3 and found that the accused being the owner of Manjunatha Lubricants and Electrical shop situated at Eeranna Gudde circle,
BSK 3rd stage without obtaining a valid license possessed Gas cylinders of various companies and the accused would refill small gas cylinders without adhering to safety measures and the accused with an intention to make wrongful gain had illegally stocked gas cylinders at sheet roof house at No. 69, 6 th Cross, 9th Main Road,
Hrishikeshnagar, Hosakerehalli.

It is further alleged that the accused had possessed gas cylinders unauthorisedly and was negligently filling gas cylinders with liquified petroleum gas and was unauthorizedly selling LPG in the market and he was also in  3  C.C.No.37139/2022 possession of LPG equipments.
Based on the said information, a case in Cr.No.246/2022 came to be registered against the accused persons.
3. After completion of the investigation, the PSI of Giri Nagara P.S. has filed chargesheet against accused for the aforesaid offences.
On receipt of charge sheet, this court took cognizance of the alleged offences.
Pursuant to the issuance and service of summons, accused entered appearance and was enlarged on bail.

The substance of accusation was read over to the accused in the language known to them, to which, the accused pleaded not guilty and submitted he has defence to make.
The plea of the accused was recorded.
Thereafter, the matter was set down for prosecution evidence.
5. In order to prove the charges, the prosecution has examined PW-1 to PW-4 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 documents.
The Statement of Accused as required U/s.313 of Cr.P.C. is recorded.
In which, the accused has denied the  4  C.C.No.37139/2022 incriminating circumstances appeared against him.
The accused has not let in either oral or documentary evidence on his behalf.
6. Heard arguments on both the sides.
I have Perused the materials on record.

7. The following points arise for my determination:-
 1)Whether the prosecution proves beyond all  reasonable doubt that on 26-08-2022 the CW-1  received credible information and conducted raid  along with CW 8 in the presence of CW 2 and 3 and  found that the accused being the owner of  Manjunatha Lubricants and Electrical shop situated  at Eeranna Gudde circle, BSK 3rd stage without  obtaining a valid license possessed Gas cylinders of  various companies and the accused would refill  small gas cylinders without adhering to safety  measures and the accused with an intention to  make wrongful gain had illegally stocked gas  cylinders at sheet roof house at No. 69, 6th Cross, 9th  Main Road, Hrishikeshnagar, Hosakerehalli and had  possessed gas cylinders unauthorisedly and was  negligently filling gas cylinders with liquified  petroleum gas and was unauthorizedly selling LPG  in the market and he was also in possession of LPG  equipments and thereby accused has committed Girinagar Police Station vs Suresh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198460357/

8. My finding to the above points are as under:-
 Point No.1 ........In the Negative.
 Point No.2..........

As per final order, for the following:-
 5  C.C.No.37139/2022  REASONS  9.
POINT No.1:-
It is the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that the prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined PW-1 to 4 and got marked Ex.P.1 to P.8 documents.
Amongst PW1 to 4, PW 2 and PW-3 being mahazar witnesses have deposed their examination in chief that they do not know anything about the incident.
They identified their signatures on Ex.P.3 as per Ex.P.3(a) and (b) and deposed that they do not know contents of Ex.P.3.
The learned Sr.APP., treated PW-2 and 3 as hostile witnesses and cross examined them.
During which PW-2 and 3 denied all other suggestions and nothing worth could be elicited from their mouth.

10. CW-1 was examined as PW-1 Deepak .L. , P.I. Hennur P.S. has deposed in his examination in chief that on 26-08-2022 when he was in station at 11.45 a.m. received information from the informant that at Eranna Gudde circle, BSK 34rd stage, the accused being owner of Manjunatha Lubricants and Electrical Girinagar Police Station vs Suresh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198460357/
4 shop, that in his shop situated at No.69, Rushikesh nagar,9th  6  C.C.No.37139/2022 main road, 6th cross accused had kept gas cylinders for domestic and Commercial purposes illegally and refilling gas to the small small cylinders without obtaining valid permit.

sentences.text: PW-1 further deposed that he called CW 2 and 3 to act as panchas and CW 4 to 7 proceeded to accused shop and found that infront of the shop and inside the shop, accused had kept gas cylinders.
CCB staff panchas conducted raid on his shop and godown, and seized item NO.1 to 11 under seizure mahazar, lodged complaint with Girinagar P.S.
He identifies the accused.

11. CW9 was examined as PW-4 Manjunatha K.D., PSI has deposed in his examination in chief that on 26-08-2022 CW-1 appeared in the station, gave complaint, seizure panchanama and material objects , based on it, he registered a case in crime No.246/2022, sent FIR to the court, he recorded statement of CW 2 to 8.
On 29-8-2022 he issued notice to the accused.
He enquired accused and arrested and released on bail, he recorded his voluntary statement.

He sent requisition to Food Inspector south zone to taking the seized material objects and on 6-9-2022 he obtained acknowledgment thereafter completion of investigation,
he submitted chargesheet against accused.
He identifies accused..

On appreciation of entire materials on record, it is apparent that the case of the prosecution is that the gas cylinders Girinagar Police Station vs Suresh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198460357/
5 were seized and the accused was arrested in the presence of the panchas.

However, in this case the panchas being PW2 and PW3 have turned hostile to the case of the prosecution and have denied the police conducting any raid and arresting the accused and also denied the police seizing of any articles in their presence.

Hence,
this court holds that the prosecution has failed to prove the arrest and seizure in this case.
In this case the prosecution had to prove that the arrest and seizure through independent witnesses.
However, the prosecution has failed to prove the same.
Hence, I give benefit of doubt to the accused and holds that the prosecution has failed to bring home the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.

 ORDER

The bail bond of accused shall be in force for a period of 6 months.
